_README: OFFLINE FALLBACK CORPUS -- SYNTHETIC DEMO DATA, NOT REAL FACT-CHECKS.
Used only when db/seed/liar/*.tsv is absent, so that `npm run db:seed` produces a
working demo without network access. Every claim, verdict, explanation and source
below was written for this project as illustrative placeholder content. The sources
are fictional ('Demo Wire Service', example.org) precisely so that nothing here can
be mistaken for a real ruling by a real organisation.
The real corpus comes from `npm run liar:fetch`, which loads the LIAR dataset

claims.text: Drinking two litres of lemon water every morning removes all toxins from the liver within a week.
claims.explanation: The liver filters blood continuously on its own; no beverage accelerates or completes that process on a weekly schedule. Lemon water contributes hydration and vitamin C, nothing more.

claims.text: The national unemployment rate has fallen for eleven consecutive quarters.
claims.explanation: The rate fell in nine of the eleven quarters cited and was flat in the other two. The direction of travel is right; the unbroken streak is not.

claims.text: Electric vehicles produce more lifetime carbon emissions than petrol cars once battery manufacturing is counted.
claims.explanation: Battery production does front-load emissions, but lifetime analyses in most grids show an electric vehicle breaking even within two to three years of typical driving and finishing well ahead.

claims.text: The city council approved the new metro line without holding a single public consultation.
claims.explanation: Three public consultations were held before the vote, with minutes published on the council's own portal.

claims.text: 5G transmission towers weaken the human immune system.
claims.explanation: 5G uses non-ionising radio frequencies far below the energy needed to affect cells. There is no mechanism by which it could suppress immune function, and no measurement showing it does.

claims.text: Government spending on public education rose by 12 percent last financial year.
claims.explanation: Nominal spending rose 12.4 percent. Adjusted for inflation the real increase was closer to 7 percent, which the claim omits.

claims.text: Vitamin C supplements prevent the common cold if taken daily.
claims.explanation: Trials show no reduction in how often healthy adults catch colds. Regular supplementation shortens duration slightly, which is a different and much smaller claim.

claims.text: More than half of the country's electricity now comes from renewable sources.
claims.explanation: Renewables exceeded half of installed generating capacity, but supplied roughly a third of actual electricity delivered. Capacity and output are not the same number.

claims.text: The new income tax slab means anyone earning under eight lakh rupees pays no tax at all.
claims.explanation: The threshold applies to taxable income after deductions, not gross salary, so a portion of earners under that gross figure still owe tax.

claims.text: Microwaving food in plastic containers destroys its nutritional value.
claims.explanation: Microwaving affects nutrients about as much as any other short cooking method, and often less. The genuine concern with some plastics is chemical migration into food, not nutrient loss.

claims.text: The water supply project was completed six months ahead of its original deadline.
claims.explanation: The contracted completion date and the commissioning certificate are both public, and the gap between them is just over six months.

claims.text: Reading on a backlit screen before bed makes it permanently harder to fall asleep.
claims.explanation: Evening screen light does delay sleep onset for many people, but the effect is temporary and reverses when the exposure stops. 'Permanently' is unsupported.

claims.text: Crime in the capital has doubled over the last two years.
claims.explanation: Total reported incidents rose about 18 percent. The doubling figure comes from one narrow category of property offence, not overall crime.

claims.text: Solar panels stop producing any power on cloudy days.
claims.explanation: Output drops, typically to between 10 and 30 percent of peak, but panels continue generating from diffuse light.

claims.text: A single tree absorbs one tonne of carbon dioxide every year.
claims.explanation: A mature broadleaf tree absorbs on the order of 20 to 25 kilograms per year. One tonne annually is off by a factor of forty or more.

claims.text: The new labour law removes the requirement for overtime pay entirely.
claims.explanation: The law changes how the overtime threshold is calculated for certain shift patterns. The obligation to pay overtime remains in the statute.

claims.text: Honey never spoils and can be eaten safely after thousands of years.
claims.explanation: Low water content and acidity make honey extraordinarily shelf-stable, and archaeological samples have been found unspoiled. Contaminated or diluted honey can still ferment.

claims.text: Online voting was used in the last general election in several districts.
claims.explanation: No district used internet voting. A small pilot allowed electronic transmission of blank ballots to overseas voters, who returned them on paper.

claims.text: Artificial sweeteners cause cancer in humans.
claims.explanation: Early rodent studies used doses far beyond human consumption. Large human cohort studies have not established a causal link at normal intake levels.

claims.text: The budget allocates more money to defence than to health and education combined.
claims.explanation: True for the central allocation alone. Counting state-level health and education spending, as this comparison usually does, reverses the ordering.

claims.text: Humans only use ten percent of their brains.
claims.explanation: Functional imaging shows activity across effectively the whole brain over the course of a day. This figure has no basis in neuroscience and never did.

claims.text: Rail fares were frozen for three years before the latest increase.
claims.explanation: Standard fares held flat for three years. A small surcharge on premium classes was introduced in the second year, which the claim glosses over.

claims.text: Charging a phone overnight permanently damages its battery.
claims.explanation: Modern charge controllers stop drawing current at full capacity. Sustained heat and very high charge levels do age cells faster, but a night on the charger is not the step change the claim implies.

claims.text: The literacy rate in the district crossed ninety percent for the first time.
claims.explanation: The latest survey records 90.4 percent, up from 88.1 percent, and prior rounds never exceeded ninety.
